name: Sage
summary: Sage (Salvia officinalis) contains cholinesterase-inhibiting terpenes with genuine nootropic data that supplement media largely ignores. RCTs include Akhondzadeh 2003 (n=39 Alzheimer's, less cognitive decline over 4 months), Wightman 2021 (n=94, working memory benefits), Scholey 2008 (n=20 older adults, secondary memory improved), and Babault 2025 (n=26 athletes, reaction time improved).
description: Canonical sage research entity for evidence and safety integration. Publication remains held until species/preparation boundaries (S. officinalis vs S. lavandulaefolia, essential oil vs extract) are explicit and thujone safety considerations are documented, passing the site's review gates.
